diagnosis: An open conductor in the subscriber drop path between the patch-panel termination and the unit 6B outlet, or at one of its terminations, is the supported cause of the isolated service loss.
reasoning: The fault is isolated to one subscriber path while the other subscribers on the same switch remain in service. The ONU and PON are online without optical alarms. Testing at Gi1/0/11 with a known-good lead establishes a stable link, showing that the switch port can provide a link under the test conditions. The open conductor between the patch-panel termination and the unit outlet, together with the failed outlet-side link test, localizes the supported fault to the subscriber drop path or its termination beyond the patch panel.
case_input: Topology: OLT PON port 0/5/4 serves building ONU C-04, connected to access switch ASW-04. Subscriber drop pair DP-11 runs from ASW-04 through a building patch panel to unit 6B. Impact: only the subscriber at unit 6B is offline; the other 31 subscribers on ASW-04 remain in service. The ONU is online, the PON shows no LOS/LOF alarm, and ASW-04 is reachable. Port Gi1/0/11, assigned to DP-11, establishes a stable link when a test laptop is connected directly at the switch using a known-good short lead. A continuity test from the patch-panel termination to the unit 6B outlet reports an open on conductor 2. A laptop connected at the unit outlet with a known-good short lead does not establish a link.
excluded_causes: A shared PON or ONU outage is inconsistent with the ONU remaining online and the other 31 subscribers remaining in service. A general ASW-04 failure is inconsistent with those subscribers retaining service and with the direct test at Gi1/0/11 establishing a stable link. The evidence does not support the switch port as the primary fault because it works with a known-good lead. A customer device fault alone does not explain the reported open conductor and failed outlet-side link test.
supporting_evidence: Only unit 6B is affected; 31 other subscribers on ASW-04 remain in service. The ONU is online and the PON has no LOS/LOF alarm. Gi1/0/11 establishes a stable link with a known-good short lead at the switch. The path from the patch-panel termination to the unit outlet tests open on conductor 2, and a laptop at the outlet does not establish a link with a known-good lead.
